title: Integral point dual models, completeness and canonical reductions
statement:
Fix the global finite-field coefficient datum with prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_n=R/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the derived category $D(R)$ of ordinary module complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and derived completeness for the ideal $(\varpi_E)$ in the multiplication-tower sense [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. Then $R[0]$ is derived complete. For every perfect $C\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], the derived dual $C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] belongs to $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(R)$ [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes] and is perfect. More precisely, if $P^\bullet$ is any bounded finite projective model of $C$, the signed complex with degree $i$ term $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^{-i},R)$ represents $C^\vee$ and has finite projective terms. For every $n\geq1$, with $-\otimes_R^LA_n:D(R)\to D(A_n)$ the derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (complexes of $R$- and $A_n$-modules regarded as modules on the ringed sites with one object), the canonical derived-Hom coefficient comparison is an isomorphism in $D(A_n)$
$$C^\vee\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C\otimes_R^LA_n,A_n).$$
If all $C\otimes_R^LA_n$ admit finite free models supported in one interval $[u,v]$, independent of $n$, all displayed dual reductions admit finite free models supported in $[-v,-u]$.

source.place: Proof Step 2: dual finite projective models, completeness and canonical reductions; returned Steps 8–10

proof.text: Use the coefficient DVR theorem to make R Noetherian and identify I=(varpi_E) with the coefficient maximal ideal. Apply finite_module_adic_complete_and_hom from [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] to the finite R-module R to obtain classical I-adic completeness. For every f in I and sequence b, form partial sums S(n,k)=sum_{j<k} f^j b(n+j). Their tails lie in I^k, so adic precompleteness supplies limits a(n). Separatedness and S(n,k+1)=b(n)+f*S(n+1,k) give a(n)-f*a(n+1)=b(n). For the kernel, iterate a(n)=f^k*a(n+k); separatedness forces a(n)=0. Thus the sequence difference map is a linear bijection. This includes f=0 and uses no arbitrary witness to define data.

source.place: Tag 091R, lemma-complete-derived-complete (geometric-series argument); coefficient valuation facts as cited

proof.text: Use the cohomology preservation of countable products in [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence]. In degree zero, conjugate the cohomology of the Roos transition arrow by the product comparison, the single-complex homology comparison, and ModuleCat.piIsoPi. Its coordinate formula is exactly the sequence difference map of Step 1. In other degrees the cohomology of every single complex is zero, so their product is zero. The transition is therefore an isomorphism on every cohomology module and hence in the derived category. The distinguished Roos triangle has zero first object. Quantify over all f in I and all derived limits to obtain [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex].

source.place: Tags 091R, lemma-complete-derived-complete; 091S, definition-derived-complete; derived.tex Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit

proof.text: For an arbitrary bounded finite projective representative P of C, use [lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model] with N=R[0]. Transport its derived Hom model along QP isomorphic to C and Q(R[0]) isomorphic to the tensor unit. Mathlib HomComplex.Cochain.toSingleEquiv identifies degree i with Hom_R(P^{-i},R), and delta_toSingleMk gives the differential (-1)^{i+1} precomposition with d_P. Module.dual_projective and Module.dual_finite give finite projective terms. The same equivalence transfers the vanishing bounds to [-b,-a]. For perfectness of the abstract dual, use the already proved upstream theorem DerivedCategory.IsPerfect.ihom_unit, whose bounded-projective definition is definitionally IsPerfectRingComplex in this localization universe.

The upstream proved DerivedCategory.IsPerfect.finite_homology and exists_homologyConcentratedIn give finite homology and bounds a,b for the perfect dual of Step 3. Take the finite set Icc(a,b); outside it either i<a or b<i and cohomology vanishes. The finite-homology proof is the Noetherian submodule and quotient argument [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-over-derived-complete-ring] to Step 2 to obtain completeness. These are exactly the three conjuncts of [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes].

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex; Tag 091S, definition-derived-complete and closure properties; algebra.tex Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation

proof.text: Use the proved upstream perfect-implies-dualizable theorem [prop-pod-biduality-at-the-point]. Choose an existing braiding on D(R) and swap the right-dual exact pairing to a left-dual exact pairing. The generic proved Functor.Monoidal.isIso_ihomComparison_app_of_exactPairing from [lem-fix-monoidal-dual-hom-comparison] makes the internal Hom comparison of any strong monoidal functor invertible at C and the unit. Compose it with the image under ihom of the monoidal unit comparison. By the definition of ihomUnitComparison this composite is precisely the canonical morphism in the statement. Apply this directly to the ordinary derived scalar reduction. No ringed-site presentation comparison and no flatness of the quotient is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A6A, lemma-base-change-RHom, clause (1) and the preceding definition of equation-base-change-RHom

proof.text: For each n, take the assumed bounded finite free representative P of the reduction. Apply the signed-dual model from Step 3 over the quotient coefficient ring, using that free modules are projective. The degree equivalence transfers Module.dual_finite and the free dual basis to finite free terms, and transfers the support bounds to [-b,-a]. Transport the model along the supplied QP isomorphism and then along the inverse of the canonical isomorphism from Step 5. This yields the required representative of the reduction of the original dual, with one common interval for all n.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q76-ca7639675 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the whole item, the guidance files (coord/dag-sync.md is absent from the snapshot), the blueprint source thm-pod-point-perfectness.proof.md Step 2 (final paragraph on duals) and the cited Stacks tags 091R, 0A66, 07VI, 0A6A and 08TC. The delivery has no new nodes, and the statement is identical to its Q136 creation. All six steps are correct. (1) O_E is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian. The geometric series inverse of Δ_f converges because the absolute value is nonarchimedean and E is complete, and the kernel is zero; f=0 also works. (2) Countable products in D(R) are termwise (lem-weil-derived-limit-existence (2)), so the Roos middle arrow is Δ_f[0], an isomorphism, and every derived limit vanishes. So R[0] is derived complete. (3) I recomputed the dual model D^i=Hom(P^{-i},R) and its sign (-1)^{i+1}. Its RHom is the 0A5W internal Hom, which is def-pur on the one-object site. (4) Finitely generated cycles, bounded support, and derived completeness from lem-sf-perfect-over-derived-complete-ring with the Step 2 input. (5) lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect gives the canonical map for any ring map, plus unitor and symmetry. (6) Interval reversal; I checked a single term, the zero complex, n=1 and negative intervals. The citer thm-pod-point-perfectness step 4 uses exactly these clauses. Batch-5: lem-pod-projective-hom-evaluation-model is generic Hom-complex algebra, and its 27-node closure has no Poincaré-duality or trace-formula proof nodes; accepted. lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented is a generic Mathlib leaf, but I replaced it with the exact leaf lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite to clear the flag. FIX: (a) B3: the statement used the derived change of rings -⊗^L_R A_n with no citation. I added [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] to the statement and stmt_deps, the same convention as lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect; the meaning is unchanged and the graph stays acyclic. (b) In step 4, replaced the trace-formula leaf in uses, text and proof_deps, and dropped its tool_uses entry.
